Garland, with 65 feet allowance, was first; and Mick Walker, with 60 feet start, gained second place. Both Finneron and Melchior, also George Powell, were non-starters, otherwise the result might have been different.

Pritchard was first with 21ft. 2in, Tom Wiley 20ft. 9in., and Micky Walker third. You will notice how our non-field event members keep popping up in the placings, so come on, you field event wallahs and do your stuff!
Bert Footer is the map-reader and pub-diviner. Micky Walker sets a standard of eating which few can hope to equal. Bert Lindsey is the court jester (perhaps he'll be "caught" one day).

Micky Walker obtained 3rd place in the handicap and will, no doubt, get much encouragement from his fine run. Several of our younger members gave sterling accounts of themselves : Beard, Rispin, Shrubb and others, who will prove their worth in later races.

When the runners were next seen, at about half distance, Carter was in the first three, together with Brown (Mitcham) and Hines (Surrey), with Penny (7th), Kemp (25th), Lucas (27th), Herbert (28th) and Mick Walker (30th) completing our scoring six.

There was a gap of 150 yards before Allum came along just ahead of Jerman, Mick Walker and Alf Shaw, with Murdock and Tobin just behind. At this point I was pleased to notice the fine style and high position of "Champ" Smith.

… as a jockey and mounted on his bucking steed, Syd Jarlett, gave us a quick Rodeo act. They were faithfully followed by Micky Walker in the rôle of stable-boy. Thus the party amused itself until it broke up at 11-30.…

We think of the disgraceful incident on Colley Hill when Harry Shields put the damper on Footer; and of a somewhat similar incident when Micky Walker saved a fiery situation on the way to Littlehampton; and of hundreds of other memorable things.

Micky Walker ran well to gain 15th place and Jimmy Green was very pleased with himself and his 19th position. "Stimmo" and Beer, both on short leave, were, however, hardly fit enough for the fast course.

At about 7 miles Sid Ring had a substantial lead, but at about 15, Richards (Mitcham) with Mick Walker in attendance, were in front. Despite every effort, Mick was unable to pass Richards, but pushed him to a record for the course, Mick being a matter of a few yards behind in 2 hrs. 49 secs., a time…
In the Poly Marathon (26 miles 385 yds.), held on a four-lap course from Chiswick Stadium, Micky Walker, nursing a gammy leg, was 8th in 3h. 8m.
Micky Walker ran a brilliant well-judged race to win by nearly four minutes in 1 hr. 59 mins. 26 secs. Sid Ring was 5th in 2.6.15 and Fred White completed the team in 8th position in 2.7.38.
Syd Warboys has moved from Essex to Wallasey, Cheshire. Mick Walker is now convalescing from an attack of pleurisy. We all hope that Mick will soon be well again.
Bob Wise ran well in the Senior 440 Yards, and Len Bishop took third place in the 1 Mile with Micky Walker, having a change from marathon running, close behind him.

Of the earlier escapades of Bert Footer, Alf Taylor, Sid Ring, Harry Shields and Micky Walker whose outsize in laughs and even larger size in appetites was the talk of the day.
Close support was given by Micky Walker (33) Bill Rice (40) Albert Shaw (43) and Cecil Penny (70) who had been brought into the team at the last moment.

Jerman was slightly unlucky not to score in a winning team in his 1st 'National'........Our other two runners, Bert Shaw (50) and Mick Walker (65) backed up well, and every one of our runners can look back upon this day of days with pleasure.
